subject: chemistry
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: In 13C NMR spectroscopy, the number of peaks equals:
options: The total number of carbon atoms
questions.explain: Each chemically distinct (non-equivalent) carbon environment produces one peak in a 13C NMR spectrum.

questions.q: Under the n+1 rule in 1H NMR, a signal that is split into a quartet is caused by:
questions.explain: A quartet arises from coupling to 3 equivalent adjacent protons, since n+1 = 3+1 = 4 lines.

questions.q: The reaction between iodide and peroxodisulfate is catalysed by Fe2+/Fe3+ because:
options: Both reactants are negative and repel; Fe ions provide an alternative route with opposite-charge steps
questions.explain: S2O8 2- and I- are both negatively charged and repel; Fe ions act as an intermediate, alternating oxidation state to lower the activation energy.

questions.q: Adding a few drops of NaOH(aq) to Fe2+(aq) produces:
questions.explain: Fe2+ gives a green precipitate of Fe(OH)2, which darkens to brown on standing as it oxidises to Fe(OH)3.

questions.q: What is the coordination number and shape of a complex ion with six monodentate ligands such as [Fe(H2O)6]2+?
questions.explain: Six monodentate ligands each donate one lone pair, giving coordination number 6 and an octahedral shape.

questions.q: The IR fingerprint region (below about 1500 cm-1) is most useful for:
options: Identifying a specific compound by matching against a database
questions.explain: The complex fingerprint region is unique to each molecule and is used to confirm identity by comparison with reference spectra.

questions.q: A compound with formula C2H6O shows two 13C peaks and, in 1H NMR, a triplet, a quartet and a broad singlet. The compound is:
questions.explain: Two carbon environments plus a CH3 triplet, CH2 quartet and exchangeable OH singlet are consistent with ethanol; dimethyl ether would give only one signal.

questions.q: How many peaks would 13C NMR show for propan-1-ol, CH3CH2CH2OH?
questions.explain: Propan-1-ol has three chemically different carbon environments, giving three peaks in the 13C NMR spectrum.

questions.q: Which definition best describes a transition metal?
options: A metal with a full d-subshell
A d-block metal that forms at least one stable ion with a partially filled d-subshell
A metal that forms only +2 ions
questions.explain: Sc and Zn are excluded because their stable ions (Sc3+, Zn2+) have empty or full d-subshells, respectively.

questions.q: The small M+1 peak in a mass spectrum arises mainly because:
options: About 1.1% of carbon atoms are the 13C isotope
Hydrogen has two isotopes in equal amounts
questions.explain: The natural abundance of 13C (about 1.1%) gives a small peak one mass unit above the molecular ion.

questions.q: Why does the [Al(H2O)6]3+ ion act as a weak acid in water?
options: The high charge density polarises coordinated water, weakening O-H bonds so H+ is released
questions.explain: The 3+ charge on the small Al3+ ion withdraws electron density from O-H bonds of ligand water, releasing H+ and lowering the pH.

questions.q: In 1H NMR, the chemical shift of a proton depends on:
options: The local electron density (degree of shielding/deshielding) around it
questions.explain: Electron-withdrawing groups deshield protons, moving signals downfield (higher ppm); shielded protons appear upfield.

questions.q: The Contact process uses V2O5 as a catalyst; this is an example of:
options: Heterogeneous catalysis using variable oxidation states (solid V2O5 reduced to V2O4 then re-oxidised by O2)
questions.explain: V2O5 oxidises SO2 and is reduced to V2O4, then re-oxidised by O2, cycling between +5 and +4 oxidation states.

questions.q: In the reaction MnO4- + 8H+ + 5Fe2+ -> Mn2+ + 4H2O + 5Fe3+, the oxidation state of manganese changes from:
questions.explain: Manganese is reduced from +7 in MnO4- to +2 in Mn2+, gaining five electrons.

questions.q: Why does scandium not behave as a typical transition metal?
options: Its only stable ion Sc3+ has an empty d-subshell
questions.explain: Sc3+ has the configuration [Ar] with no d-electrons, so it lacks the partially filled d-subshell needed for characteristic transition-metal behaviour.

questions.q: Silicon dioxide, SiO2, when classified by its acid-base behaviour is best described as:
options: An acidic oxide that is insoluble in water but reacts with hot concentrated alkali
An amphoteric oxide that dissolves in acid
questions.explain: SiO2 is acidic, reacting with hot concentrated NaOH to form a silicate, though it is insoluble in water.

questions.q: Why are most aqueous transition-metal ions coloured?
options: The metals emit light by nuclear decay
s-electrons are excited to higher p-orbitals
Electrons are promoted between split d-orbitals, absorbing certain wavelengths of visible light
questions.explain: Ligands split the d-orbitals; absorption of visible light promotes a d-electron, and the complementary colour is transmitted.

questions.q: An IR spectrum shows a strong broad absorption near 3300 cm-1 and one near 1050 cm-1, with no peak near 1700 cm-1. The compound is most likely a(n):
questions.explain: The broad O-H stretch with a C-O stretch and no C=O peak indicates an alcohol rather than an acid or carbonyl compound.

questions.q: Dimethyl ether (CH3OCH3) and ethanol (C2H6O) can be distinguished by 13C NMR because dimethyl ether shows:
options: One peak (the two carbons are equivalent)
questions.explain: In CH3OCH3 the two methyl carbons are equivalent by symmetry, giving a single 13C peak, unlike ethanol's two peaks.

questions.q: Which IR absorption is characteristic of a carbonyl (C=O) group?
questions.explain: The C=O stretch produces a strong absorption at approximately 1680-1750 cm-1.

questions.q: Which Period 3 oxide gives the most acidic solution when added to water?
questions.explain: SO3 reacts with water to form sulfuric acid, a strong acid, giving the lowest pH of the Period 3 oxides.

questions.q: EDTA4- is described as a hexadentate ligand because it can:
options: Replace six water molecules with six EDTA ions
Donate lone pairs from six atoms to one metal ion
questions.explain: EDTA4- donates electron pairs from two nitrogen and four oxygen atoms, bonding to the metal through six coordinate bonds.

questions.q: Which factor would change the colour (wavelength absorbed) of a transition-metal complex?
options: Changing the volume of solvent only
questions.explain: Different ligands cause different d-orbital splitting energies, altering the wavelength absorbed and hence the observed colour.

questions.q: In thin-layer chromatography (TLC), the Rf value is calculated as:
options: Mass of spot / mass of solvent
Distance moved by spot / distance moved by solvent
Distance moved by solvent / distance moved by spot
questions.explain: Rf = distance travelled by the component divided by the distance travelled by the solvent front.

questions.q: A solution of [V(H2O)6]2+ is violet. The colour we see is:
options: The complementary colour of the wavelength absorbed
questions.explain: The transmitted/observed colour is complementary to the wavelengths of visible light that the complex absorbs.

questions.q: Why is dilute sulfuric acid, rather than HCl, used to acidify manganate(VII) titrations?
options: Chloride ions would be oxidised by MnO4-, giving a false result
questions.explain: MnO4- would oxidise Cl- to Cl2, consuming extra MnO4- and over-reading the titre, so non-oxidisable H2SO4 is used.

questions.q: Why are manganate(VII) titrations self-indicating?
options: The purple MnO4- is decolourised, and the first excess drop turns the solution pink
The Mn2+ product is intensely coloured
questions.explain: MnO4- is decolourised as it reacts; the endpoint is the first permanent pale pink from a slight excess of MnO4-.

questions.q: Which species is responsible for the deep blue colour formed when excess ammonia is added to copper(II) sulfate solution?
questions.explain: Ammonia partially substitutes water to give the deep blue [Cu(NH3)4(H2O)2]2+ ion.

questions.q: Adding excess aqueous ammonia to Cu2+(aq) (after initial precipitate) gives:
options: A pale blue precipitate that stays
A deep blue solution as the precipitate dissolves
questions.explain: Excess NH3 acts as a ligand, dissolving Cu(OH)2 to form the deep blue [Cu(NH3)4(H2O)2]2+ complex.

questions.q: In gas chromatography (GC), the time a component takes to pass through the column to the detector is called the:
questions.explain: Retention time is the characteristic time a component takes to travel through the GC column and reach the detector.
